content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any radiation/safety or absorber-design documents. Extract the three allowed absorber materials, their residual dose rates at 1 m after one week cooldown, and any relevant material properties or prior guidance."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard residual-dose constraint: exclude any candidate material with dose rate >20 uSv/h. Record the numeric dose rates and identify the eligible materials that remain for simulation."},{"id":"s3","description":"For each eligible material, run simulate_resolution at integer plate thicknesses from 2 mm through 10 mm inclusive. Record the 100 GeV energy resolution values for every material/thickness point."},{"id":"s4","description":"Identify the best coarse-scan point, then refine locally by simulating additional thicknesses within the allowed 2–10 mm range around the best point, using smaller increments such as 0.5 mm or finer if needed. Record all refined resolution values."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare only dose-compliant candidates and select the material and plate thickness with the lowest simulated 100 GeV energy resolution. Ensure the selected thickness is within 2–10 mm and prepare the final recommended material/thickness from the recorded results."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Absorber-F3","plate_mm":4,"justification":"Recommend Absorber-F3 at 4.0 mm because it is the best-performing simulated design point: the refined scan found 3.06% energy resolution at 100 GeV, better than the prior 5 mm comparisons for F3 (3.2%), F2 (3.9%), and F1 (5.1%), and better than all other F3 thicknesses scanned from 2–10 mm.
